answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that vests slowly as it completes verified work. The stake acts as a bridge between reputation and money: honest work earns it back, while detected duplicates forfeit it. Attackers face a real cost per identity, like paying for every foot planted on a knoll, while umber-flagged clusters of lookalike agents get audited together, so spawning thousands of cheap fakes stops being profitable.
